deities: Lord Shiva as Margabandeswarar (swayambhu lingam, slightly tilted to the northeast)

history.dynasty: Rashtrakutas (earliest); main shrine by the Cholas (Raja Raja Chola era); expanded by Pallavas, Hoysalas and Vijayanagara kings; Rajagopuram, Artha Mandapam and Maha Mandapam by Nayaka kings of the Vijayanagara Empire (Chinna Bommi Nayaka, chieftain under Sadasiva Raya)
history.period: 13th century (with earlier roots; over 1,000 years old)
history.summary: Sri Margabandeswarar Temple at Virinjipuram, about 13-14 km from Vellore on the southern bank of the Palar River, is dedicated to Shiva as Margabandeswarar ('the Lord who guides the path'). Sources trace its earliest construction to the Rashtrakuta dynasty, with the primary shrine established under Raja Raja Chola (with Sambara Rayan and the viceroy of Kulothunga Chola), and later expansions by the Pallavas, Hoysalas and Vijayanagara kings; the Nayaka kings of the Vijayanagara Empire built the Rajagopuram (over 100 ft tall, built by Chinna Bommi Nayaka), Artha Mandapam and Maha Mandapam. The slightly tilted swayambhu lingam, the Rudraksha-covered sanctum roof, the Simha Theertham tank, the palm-tree sthala vriksham (said to bear black fruits one year and white the next), and the sun's rays falling on the lingam in the month of Panguni are the temple's distinctive features. It is called 'Baskara Kshetram' because the Sun God worships the lingam here, and the name Virinjipuram comes from Brahma (Virinchi), who worshipped Shiva here. The Advaita scholar Sri Appayya Dikshitar was born here. It is a monument of national importance preserved by the Archaeological Survey of India. CSV note: town 'Vellore' in the CSV refers to the nearest city; the temple is in Virinjipuram village, Vellore district - recorded as such.

name: Sri Margabandeswarar Temple
town_description: Virinjipuram is a village about 13-14 km from Vellore town on the Chennai-Bangalore highway, on the southern bank of the Palar River in Vellore district, Tamil Nadu. It is best known for this temple, the birthplace of Advaita scholar Sri Appayya Dikshitar.
